requirement:
`habeas coverage-check` MUST check saved execution coverage against
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions`, returning success only when
every applicable obligation is satisfied or has accepted exception evidence
under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. The command MUST NOT
build the project, execute tests, collect coverage, or invoke an assessment model.
rationale:
structural: No structural obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.check` or its refining requirements needs implementation evidence. None of them has an implementation edge, and the review roots are empty. I judged each candidate clause by asking whether a different implementation could give the same observable behavior and still break the clause.

- **`requirements.test-coverage.check`**
  - Clause: "`habeas coverage-check` MUST check saved execution coverage against ... threshold ... and ... functions, returning success only when every applicable obligation is satisfied or has accepted exception evidence".
    - This is the command's observable outcome. Any internal structure that produces the same outcome satisfies it.
  - Clause: "MUST NOT build the project, execute tests, collect coverage, or invoke an assessment model".
    - This is a behavioral prohibition on what the command does. It prescribes no type, signature, library or delegation.
- **`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`**
  - Clauses: the 80% target, the file-and-line union counting rule, "exact counts rather than rounded displayed percentages", no per-function 80% target, not-measured files requiring an exception, and the no-executable-obligations report.
    - These all describe results and decisions.
  - Clause: "MUST use the combined selection and freshness rules of `requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and `requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`".
    - This names rules to follow. It doesn't name a function, interface or module that must be called.
    - An implementation that reproduced the same selection and freshness behavior without calling shared code would give identical results.
- **`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions`**
  - Clauses: every function without attributable execution needs an exception, and nested functions or closures must not count toward the enclosing function.
    - These constrain which results are reported, not how the code is built.
- **`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`**
  - Clauses: exceptions must be current, accepted and independently assessed, attached to the specific file or function, and invalidated when citation-review inputs change. Function and gap identities must stay portable across checkouts.
    - These constrain the evidence semantics and the identity values.
    - They don't prescribe a field, type or interface. Another representation with the same attachment, invalidation and portability behavior would conform.

Every clause therefore specifies observable behavior, and the implementation choices behind it are discretionary. Whether the behavior is tested is a separate question for the behavioral criterion.

behavioral: Obligations in `requirements.test-coverage.check` and the tests that cover them:

1. **Check saved coverage against the threshold and function requirements.**
   - The unit tests `mod[tests]/fn[accepted_file_and_function_explanations_remain_separate_from_execution]` and `mod[tests]/fn[missing_and_stale_explanations_fail_the_report]` in `src/execution_coverage/check.rs` use recorded runs. They assert that 0/1 coverage fails and that a zero-execution function fails.
   - The integration test `fn[full_test_flow_checks_real_function_counters_after_all_tests]` in `tests/execution_coverage.rs` runs real coverage followed by `habeas coverage-check` on saved data. It asserts success ('Coverage check passed') for a covered project.
   - The same test asserts failure ('Coverage check failed') and reports `#fn[outer]/fn[hidden]: zero execution` when a nested function is unexecuted. It also asserts the enclosing `#fn[outer]` is not flagged, which covers the nested/enclosing function rule.

2. **Success only when every obligation is satisfied or has accepted exception evidence.**
   - The unit tests cover a missing review, a `false` review, a `{fixme}` determination, a stale file citation, a changed citation, and a changed outline input. All of these fail the report.
   - A `true` review passes. File and function exceptions stay separate, and a file exception does not waive a function.
   - An unmeasured file and unmeasured functions are accepted only through the exception.
   - A citation that is no longer needed does not break a passing report.

3. **The command MUST NOT build, execute tests, collect coverage, or invoke a model.**
   - `fn[book_rendering_preserves_retained_coverage_and_never_launches_tests]` runs the standalone `coverage-check` with a fake `cargo` on `PATH`. The fake cargo records any call other than `metadata` and exits 99.
   - It asserts that the test-executed marker file was not created, that no forbidden command ran, and that the retained coverage storage is unchanged.
   - The full-flow test uses `model_tripwire`, which configures a trap model endpoint in `habeas.toml`. It runs `saved_check` and asserts zero model requests. It also asserts the `evidence` directory is unchanged.

The detailed threshold rules, function rules and exception rules belong to the cited requirements `.threshold`, `.functions` and `.exceptions`. Those are context here and are not reassessed. The tests also exercise applying them in this subject's cases.

I found no behavioral obligation without a test.

text: :::{req} check
`habeas coverage-check` MUST check saved execution coverage against
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions`, returning success only when
every applicable obligation is satisfied or has accepted exception evidence
under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. The command MUST NOT
build the project, execute tests, collect coverage, or invoke an assessment model.
:::{req} check.threshold
Each first-party Rust file under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing` MUST have at least 80%
execution coverage of its instrumented lines, or current accepted exception
evidence explaining why the file falls below that target under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Counts MUST use the
file-and-line union rule of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`;
a line counts as executed when any eligible test process or its associated
child processes has a positive execution count for it.
The check MUST use the combined selection and freshness rules of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, restricted to the active
build configuration. It MUST compare exact counts rather than rounded displayed
percentages, average file percentages, or impose an 80% target within each
function. A file whose executable code is not measured MUST require exception
evidence rather than pass with a fabricated percentage. A file established to
contain no executable coverage obligations MUST be reported as such and MUST
NOT require a threshold exception.
Absence of recorded instrumented lines alone MUST NOT establish that a file
contains no executable coverage obligations.
:::{req} check.functions
Every function under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.scope` without
recorded execution attributable to it MUST have current accepted exception
evidence under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`, even when
its containing file meets the target of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`.
Execution attributable only to another function, including a nested function
or closure, MUST NOT establish coverage of the enclosing function merely
because their source locations overlap. Having no recorded lines alone MUST
NOT establish that a function has no executable coverage obligations.
:::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
